q-82985.name: Question 1
q-82985.problem:
Using the change of variables $u=x+3y$ and $v=x+2y,$ evaluate the double integral

$$
{∬}_{D}\frac{x+3y}{x+2y}\,dx\,dy,
$$

where $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x+3y\le 2,\,2\le x+2y\le 4\}.$
q-82985.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|du\,dv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+3y,\,v=x+2y
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,2\le v\le 4\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & \text{ }\text{ }2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=-1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{x+3y}{x+2y}\,dx\,dy & ={∬}_{Δ}\frac{u}{v}\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}\frac{u}{v}\cdot |-1|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{u}{v}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}u[{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{v}\,dv]du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}u[\operatorname{ln}⁡v]_{2}^{4}\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}u(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\,du \\  & =(2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡2){\int }_{0}^{2}u\,du \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot (2-0) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-160899.problem:
Using the change of variables $u=\frac{y}{x}$ and $v=xy,$ evaluate the double integral

$$
{∬}_{D}{e}^{-xy/2}\,dx\,dy,
$$

where $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{x}{4}\le y\le 2x,\,1\le xy\le 4\}.$
q-160899.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|du\,dv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{x},\,v=xy
$$

 
gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v)\,:\,\frac{1}{4}\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le 4\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \frac{1}{x} \\ y & \text{ }\text{ }x\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\frac{2y}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{(-\frac{2y}{x})}=-\frac{1}{2u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{-xy/2}\,dx\,dy & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{-v/2}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{-v/2}\cdot |-\frac{1}{2u}|\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{1/4}^{2}\frac{{e}^{-v/2}}{u}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{-v/2}[{\int }_{1/4}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{-v/2}[\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|\,{|}_{1/4}^{2}]du \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{-v/2}[\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{1}{4}]\,du \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{-v/2}\,du \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\cdot {[-2{e}^{-v/2}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot ({e}^{-2}-{e}^{-1/2}) \\  & =3({e}^{-1/2}-{e}^{-2})\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
u=x+y,\,v=x-y

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$

$$

$$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & \text{ }\text{ }-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}

q-38371.problem:
Using the change of variables $u=xy$ and $v=y+x,$ evaluate the double integral

$$
{∬}_{D}|y-x|\,{e}^{xy}\,dxdy,
$$

where $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le xy\le 4,\,1\le y+x\le 10\}.$
q-38371.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dxdy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=xy,\,v=y+x
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 4,\,1\le v\le 10\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =y-x.\end{aligned}
$$

.

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{y-x}
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}|y-x|\,{e}^{xy}\,dxdy & ={∬}_{Δ}|y-x|\,{e}^{u}\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}|y-x|\,{e}^{u}\,\frac{1}{|y-x|}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}[{\int }_{1}^{10}{e}^{u}\,dv]du \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}[{\int }_{1}^{10}dv]du \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}[v]_{1}^{10}\,du \\  & =9{\int }_{1}^{4}{e}^{u}\,du \\  & =9[{e}^{u}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =9({e}^{4}-e).\end{aligned}
$$
